summary: This bill establishes a tax on greenhouse gas emissions from fossil fuels, industrial processes, and certain products, using the generated revenue to fund infrastructure projects, energy worker assistance, and other environmental initiatives, while also creating a National Climate Commission to set emissions reduction goals and review federal policies.

scores.thoughts: Title I establishes the 'Rebuilding Infrastructure and Solutions for the Environment Trust Fund' (RISE Trust Fund) which appropriates and transfers 75% of new greenhouse gas tax revenues. This fund then allocates significant percentages to various federal programs and trust funds, including 70% to the Highway Trust Fund, 2.5% to the Airport and Airway Trust Fund, and other percentages to environmental, energy, and worker assistance programs. Title II also appropriates additional funds for cancer research. These provisions clearly indicate a substantial increase in government spending across multiple sectors, funded by new taxes.

Title I of the bill introduces a new subtitle to the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, imposing a tax on greenhouse gas emissions from combusted fossil fuels, industrial processes, and certain product uses. The bill also repeals federal motor vehicle and aviation fuel taxes, but the new greenhouse gas taxes are a significant new revenue source. The primary purpose of Title I is to establish this new tax system.

Title IV of the bill explicitly establishes a 'National Bipartisan Fiscal Commission' with the duty to 'review and recommend a legislative package for Congress to stabilize long-term deficits and debt'. This indicates a direct focus on prioritizing debt reduction, even though other parts of the bill involve new spending and taxation. The commission's mandate is central to this topic.
